title: Police officers being investigated
article: Halton Regional Police are probing a potential connection between the murder of a woman in West Oak Trails Thursday and the fatal shooting of a man outside an Oakville police station hours later.
The province's Special Investigations Unit is investigating whether Halton Regional Police officers should be charged after a man was shot dead before noon.

The fatal police shooting took place around 11:35 a.m. when police found "an individual causing damage to the parking lot" at the police station on Oak Walk Dr., in the area of Dundas St. and Trafalgar Rd.
An incident followed with several police officers, resulting in the man being shot dead.
No officers were injured.
SIU spokesperson Monica Hudon said she didn't have the age of the dead man or where he resided, and didn't yet know how many officers have been designated the subjects of the investigation.
Meanwhile, Halton Police are investigating a second crime scene in Oakville that may be connected to Thursday's deadly shooting.
Homicide officers are at a home on Treetop Terrace, in the area of Westoak Trails Blvd. and Upper Middle Rd., where the body of a female was reportedly found inside a townhouse.
Hudon wouldn't confirm or deny a connection, adding only that the SIU is "solely investigating the actions of officers" in the police station incident.
Halton Police also would neither confirm nor deny a connection.

A Treetop Terrace neighbour, who only gave her name as Lorraine, said a mother of two boys, believed to be eight and nine-years-old, lived in the townhouse. She said the family moved to the neighbourhood last summer and were very quiet.
Robert, a man who owns a landscaping company across the street, witnessed the police incident.
He said he heard about 10 shots ring out and saw a man in a car get out while the vehicle was still moving. The man was approached by three officers with their weapons drawn.
Robert said the man collapsed on the ground and then several other officers ran out of the building towards the scene.
Halton Paramedics tried tirelessly to revive the man at the scene.
Sgt. Dave Cross of Halton Police told reporters "that it is disturbing" that this incident happened steps from the Halton Police station.
The parking lot was taped off by investigators and the body was surrounded by police cruisers for several hours.

Approximately five metres from the body sits a grey Nissan Altima with a smashed right front bender; the driver's door is also ajar. A Halton police van that has damage to its right side is also nearby. It appears that a collision took place prior to the shooting.
The Nissan is a rental car from Enterprise.
Police say the station opened less than three years ago.
The SIU gets involved in a case whenever a civilian is assaulted, seriously injured or killed while in the presence of police, to determine whether criminal charges are warranted.
-with files from Torstar
